title: Radiosynthesis and evaluation of a fluorine-18 labeled radioligand targeting vesicular acetylcholine transporter.
abstract: Vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT) is a reliable biomarker for assessing the loss of cholinergic neurons in the brain that is associated with cognitive impairment of patients. 5-Hydrotetralin compound (±)-5-OH-VAT is potent (K<sub>i</sub> = 4.64 ± 0.32 nM) and selective for VAChT (>1800-fold and 398-fold for σ<sub>1</sub> and σ<sub>2</sub> receptor, respectively) with favorable hydrophilicity (LogD = 1.78), while (-)-5-OH-VAT originally serves as the radiolabeling precursor of (-)-[<sup>18</sup>F]VAT, a promising VAChT radiotracer with a logD value of 2.56. To evaluate (-)-5-OH-[<sup>18</sup>F]VAT as a radiotracer for VAChT, we performed in vitro binding assay to determine the potency of the minus enantiomer (-)-5-OH-VAT and plus enantiomer (+)-5-OH-VAT, indicating that (-)-5-OH-VAT is a more potent VAChT enantiomer. Radiosynthesis of (-)-5-OH-[<sup>18</sup>F]VAT was explored using three strategies. (-)-5-OH-[<sup>18</sup>F]VAT was achieved with a good yield (24 ± 6%) and high molar activity (∼37 GBq/µmol, at the end of synthesis) using a microwave assisted two-step one-pot procedure that started with di-MOM protected nitro-containing precursor (-)-6. MicroPET studies in the brain of nonhuman primate (NHP) suggest that (-)-5-OH-[<sup>18</sup>F]VAT readily penetrated the blood brain barrier and specifically accumulated in the VAChT-enriched striatum with improved washout kinetics from striatum compared to [<sup>18</sup>F]VAT. Nevertheless, the lower target to non-target ratio may limit its use for in vivo measurement of the VAChT level in the brain.
